newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares mixed, Gazprom lower on uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares mixed, Gazprom lower on uncertainty.

text.p: Controversy over share ownership rules for Russian natural gas producer Gazprom depressed its shares on Wednesday, and traders said the market was declining despite some interest in second tier stocks.
Traders said that uncertainty over a decree on local Gazprom share ownership said to be under presidential consideration was adversely affecting Gazprom shares.
"They've completely messed up, making (local Gazprom shares) more unattractive for investors," a trader at a Western brokerage said.
Gazprom traded at $0.640 at 1330 GMT, up from a morning low of $0.620 but down from $0.653 on Tuesday on $21.8 million turnover, about as much as the rest of the market put together.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index had fallen to 351.73 at 1200 GMT from 355.30 at Tuesday's close. Benchmark UES slipped to $0.3117 from $0.3170.

"There's a constant demand for second- and third-tier stock, but overall the market is aimed downwards, despite the fact it went up a little bit (this afternoon)," said Rinaco Plus trader Valery Levit.
He said prices had not yet reached a level attractive to buyers and Western investors were hardly buying at all.

Energy Minister Boris Nemtsov's spokesman denied rumours that foreigners would be forced to sell local Gazprom shares, which gave the price some support, but confusion over what a presidential decree regulating ownership would order remained.
"The local market is going to see cheaper prices on underlying shares and ADRs are going to go up...because ADRs are not affected," the trader at the Western brokerage said.
Traders noted a few major buying orders on individual leading shares which boosted prices in regional power utility Mosenergo and Russia's biggest oil producer LUKoil in the second half of the day.
Mosenergo rose to $1.271 after closing on Tuesday at $1.267 while LUKoil climbed to $14.79 from $14.67.
